hero.headline: Golden Knights, Hurricanes to meet in Stanley Cup Final starting June 2
hero.body:
The NHL announced the Vegas Golden Knights will face the Carolina Hurricanes in the Stanley Cup Final, with Game 1 scheduled for June 2. The league also listed June 4 as a potential start date.

The series marks the Golden Knights' return to the championship round as they seek another title. Carolina will host the opening games of the series.

The NHL finalized the schedule after both conference finals concluded. The matchup brings together two teams that advanced through their respective playoff brackets to reach hockey's biggest stage.

The Hurricanes earned home-ice advantage for the first two games of the series. The exact game times and complete series schedule were released by the league alongside the announcement.

Both teams now have several days to prepare for the championship series. The Golden Knights previously competed in the Stanley Cup Final during their inaugural season in 2018, losing to the Washington Capitals. They won their first championship in 2023.

The Hurricanes last appeared in the Stanley Cup Final in 2006, when they defeated the Edmonton Oilers to claim the franchise's only championship. The team relocated from Hartford to Carolina in 1997.

The series will follow the standard 2-2-1-1-1 format, with Carolina hosting Games 1 and 2 before the series shifts to Vegas. If necessary, additional games would alternate between the two cities.

Vegas advanced through the Western Conference playoffs to reach the final, while Carolina won the Eastern Conference. Both teams completed their conference final series in time for the league to set the June 2 start date for the championship round.

cards.headline: Americans Injured in Iranian Missile Strike on Kuwaiti Air Base
cards.body:
American personnel were wounded when Iran launched missiles at a military facility in Kuwait, according to US Central Command. The attack happened just hours after the US and Iran had reached agreement on a framework to halt the escalating conflict.

The strike targeted a Kuwaiti base hosting American forces. US officials characterized it as a serious breach of the ceasefire negotiations that had been under discussion.

President Trump was preparing to make a final decision on a proposed two-month extension to pause the fighting with Iran. He spent two hours at the White House meeting with advisers to discuss the matter, according to a senior administration official. Trump had previously indicated on social media that he was ready to announce his determination.

The presidential meeting concluded without any deal announcement. While US and Iranian officials had previously confirmed they had agreed on a framework for a potential agreement, the missile attack raised questions about whether any arrangement could hold.

The strike reflects broader regional tensions. Shipping data shows that vessels have been attempting to exit the Strait of Hormuz with their tracking systems disabled. About a quarter of the large oil tankers caught in the conflict have successfully left the area.

Passage through the strait has declined significantly as efforts to reopen the waterway have made slow progress. More non-Iranian vessels are now crossing the Strait of Hormuz compared to earlier in the conflict, according to the available data.

US Central Command issued a statement characterizing the Iranian missile launch as egregious aggression. The strike on Kuwait appeared to follow recent US targeting operations against Iran.

The attack highlights how fragile the ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain. Trump had been considering a proposal to extend the pause in fighting for two months, but Iran's latest military action complicates those discussions significantly.

The timing of the assault raised questions about Iran's intentions in the ongoing negotiations. The strike came hours after the two sides had made progress toward an agreement, suggesting Iran may have been testing whether the US would maintain its commitment to talks despite the military action.

US officials indicated they would need to reassess their approach following the attack. The incident added pressure on Trump to decide whether to continue pursuing diplomacy or take a harder line in response to Iranian aggression.

The violence underscores how quickly the situation in the region can shift and how vulnerable any agreement remains to military actions by either side. Both nations have indicated they prefer a negotiated solution, yet their military operations continue to test whether peace is achievable.

cards.headline: Pentagon chief says US ready to resume strikes on Iran without deal
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States is prepared to restart military operations against Iran if negotiations fail to produce an agreement.
cards.body:
Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said the US is prepared to resume military strikes against Iran if negotiations fail. He emphasized that the country has the capability to restart conflict while the Trump administration pursues diplomatic efforts.

This statement comes as the US and Iran work toward a framework agreement. Trump met with advisers to make a final determination on the deal, which would address reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's uranium program. Recent strikes between the two countries have raised questions about how military escalation might affect prospects for reaching an agreement.

cards.headline: Germany Deploys Troops to Lithuania Amid Fears of Russian Aggression
cards.teaser: Berlin has stationed forces in the Baltic country to provide protection against potential Russian threats in Europe.
cards.body:
Germany has deployed military forces to Lithuania to bolster the Baltic nation's security against potential Russian aggression. Lithuanian authorities welcomed the deployment, marking a significant shift in the historical relationship between the two countries.

The move carries symbolic weight given that Lithuania was occupied by Germany during World War II. Today, German troops are stationed in Lithuania as allies addressing contemporary security concerns about Russian intentions in the Baltic region.

cards.headline: Nine confirmed dead in Longview paper mill chemical tank disaster
cards.body:
A chemical tank rupture at a paper mill in Longview, Washington has claimed nine lives, with two workers still missing and presumed dead. Recovery crews continued operations at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co facility on Friday after finding additional remains.

The disaster occurred when an industrial tank holding approximately 600,000 gallons of white liquor ruptured on Tuesday morning. White liquor is a caustic chemical mixture containing sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide, used in the kraft paper manufacturing process to break down wood fibers.

"We're bracing ourselves for this being the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history," said Washington Governor Bob Ferguson at a news conference Wednesday.

Recovery operations began Wednesday following delays caused by concerns about the structural integrity of the damaged tank. Authorities transitioned from rescue efforts to recovery, indicating no hope of finding additional survivors. Matt Amos with the Longview fire department said operations would proceed "slow, methodical and deliberate," with recovered victims undergoing decontamination before being transported to the coroner's office. Seven workers remained hospitalized with severe burns from exposure to the chemical.

The U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board announced a federal investigation into the incident. The cause of the tank failure remained under investigation, with authorities saying there was no immediate threat to the surrounding community of about 40,000 residents.

The spillage from the rupture flowed into drainage ditches and contaminated the nearby Columbia River. Dead carp were discovered following the incident. About 25,000 gallons of white liquor continued to slowly leak from the tank. The Washington Department of Ecology and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency oversaw operations to determine environmental impacts. Authorities warned the public to avoid ditches and dikes while testing continued, though they reported no air quality or drinking water concerns in Longview.

The sprawling Nippon Dynawave facility employs approximately 1,000 people and produces materials for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates and cartons. The plant sits along the Columbia River adjacent to other timber, paper and chemical businesses in this mill town.

Brian Wood, representing Nippon Dynawave, a subsidiary of Japan-based Nippon Paper Group, said the company was focused on the victims and would cooperate fully with the investigation. "These are our people," he stated during a Wednesday news conference.

Safety complaints had been filed against the company in March and May, though the state's labor and industries department said both were unrelated to the current situation. Since the start of 2021, the company had been fined 3,400 dollars for three separate health and safety violations.

At a community vigil Tuesday night, dozens of residents gathered to pray and light candles. Many remained waiting for answers about missing coworkers and friends. "There's families that have been torn apart, and we don't know why," said Longview resident Crystal Moldenhauer.

cards.headline: Oil prices drop sharply on signs of U.S.-Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices fell and recorded the biggest monthly decline in six years as investors anticipated a potential U.S.-Iran deal.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell sharply Thursday after reports emerged of a potential breakthrough in U.S.-Iran talks that could extend a ceasefire. The decline reflects market expectations that an agreement might increase Iranian oil supplies, easing global supply constraints.

The price drops contributed to oil's largest monthly decline since 2020. Brent crude posted its worst month in several years, providing some relief to consumers at the pump as traders weighed the implications of the potential deal.

cards.headline: Vietnamese Leader Warns Against Superpower Conflict in Asia
cards.teaser: Vietnam's leader To Lam told regional military leaders that distrust and disregard for established rules have created dangerous conditions in Asia.
cards.body:
Vietnamese leader To Lam addressed military leaders from across Asia, warning about the risks posed by superpower competition. He said that distrust and a lack of respect for established rules had created what he described as a culture of the big fish swallowing the small fish.

Lam delivered the remarks in a speech focused on regional security dynamics. His comments reflected growing concerns among smaller Asian nations about being caught between competing major powers in the region.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border with Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola Outbreak Grows
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as suspected cases of a rare form of Ebola continue to surge.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo following a growing Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain of Ebola. The outbreak has expanded in the DRC, prompting Uganda to implement border closure measures to prevent further spread.

The World Health Organization estimates the death rate between 30% and 50% among confirmed cases. WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus traveled to the DRC capital, Kinshasa, to support containment efforts. The organization called for a ceasefire among armed groups to help prevent deaths from the preventable disease.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth Says US Expects Asian Allies to Increase Defense Spending
cards.teaser: The US defense secretary told an Asian security summit in Singapore that America is not turning back on its regional allies but expects greater defense contributions.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Hegseth addressed concerns about US commitment to Asia at a security summit in Singapore, asserting that the United States is not abandoning its regional allies. He emphasized that the US expects these partners to increase their defense spending and take on greater responsibility for regional security.

Hegseth discussed further arms deals with Asian nations and criticized China's regional activities during the forum, which brought together military leaders from across the continent.

cards.headline: Spain's Prime Minister Faces Survival Fight Amid Multiple Corruption Probes
cards.teaser: Pedro Sánchez confronts investigations into colleagues and relatives after eight years leading the Spanish government.
cards.body:
Spain's Sánchez digs in after eight years as PM as wave of scandals threatens survival

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez faces a critical political moment as corruption investigations expand to include members of his inner circle and family. After eight years leading the country, the premier must navigate multiple simultaneous probes that observers view as a test of his political survival.

The scandals sweeping through Sánchez's political and personal orbit have intensified scrutiny on his leadership. His ability to maintain power now depends on how these investigations unfold.

cards.headline: Japan's Immigration Crackdown Forces Foreign Curry Shop Owners to Leave
cards.teaser: New visa rules under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are affecting foreign business owners who have established lives in Japan.
cards.body:
New immigration rules implemented under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi are forcing some foreign business owners to leave Japan. Curry shop proprietors have been particularly affected by the visa policy changes.

The crackdown impacts foreign entrepreneurs who had put down roots in the country and built their businesses over time. The stricter visa requirements represent a shift in Japan's approach to foreign residents engaged in small business operations.

cards.headline: Judge orders Trump name removed from Kennedy Center
cards.teaser: A federal judge ordered the removal of Trump's name from the Kennedy Center building and blocked attempts to close or rename the cultural institution.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered that Trump's name be removed from the Kennedy Center. The ruling also prevents the performing arts venue from closing or changing its name, blocking Trump's announced plan for a two-year closure to conduct extensive renovations.

Trump responded to the court decision by stating he has no interest in the Kennedy Center following the judge's order. The decision ensures the center will remain open and continue operating under its current name.

cards.headline: Louisiana passes congressional map eliminating majority-Black district
cards.teaser: Louisiana lawmakers approved a new congressional map that eliminates a majority-Black district, with Republicans pushing through the redistricting plan.
cards.body:
Louisiana's Republican-controlled legislature approved a new congressional map that dismantles one of the state's two majority-Black districts. The move came after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled the previous map unconstitutional in a sweeping decision.

The redistricting plan favors Republican candidates in future elections while reducing Black voting power in the state's congressional representation.

cards.headline: Trump meeting on Iran deal ends without announcement
cards.teaser: President Trump concluded a Situation Room meeting with advisers on a potential Iran deal without making a final determination, despite earlier reports of a framework agreement.
cards.body:
Trump held a meeting at the White House with his advisers to make a final determination on a potential deal with Iran. Officials had confirmed that the US and Iran agreed on a framework for a deal involving reopening the Strait of Hormuz and destroying uranium.

No announcement was made following the meeting. The Pentagon said the US was prepared to resume strikes on Iran if negotiations failed to produce an agreement.

cards.headline: Pentagon chief says US ready to resume strikes on Iran without deal
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States is prepared to restart military operations against Iran if negotiations fail to produce an agreement.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Former Attorney General Bondi addresses Epstein files redaction errors
cards.teaser: Pam Bondi told lawmakers that redaction errors occurred in the release of Epstein files and placed responsibility on other officials.
cards.body:
Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before lawmakers about redaction errors in the release of Epstein files. During her testimony, Bondi attributed responsibility for the mistakes to Todd Blanche and Kash Patel.

Bondi distanced herself from the handling of the files during questioning. Her testimony shifted focus to Blanche, making him a target for Democrats seeking accountability for how the documents were released with improper redactions.

cards.headline: White House releases Trump physical exam results
cards.teaser: Trump's doctor said the president is in excellent health and fully fit to serve, while recommending weight loss and more exercise.
cards.body:
Trump's physician released results stating the president is in excellent health and fully fit to serve. The doctor recommended that Trump lose weight and exercise more as part of routine health guidance.

The physical exam noted leg swelling and hand bruising. The White House released the results after Trump underwent his latest physical examination at Walter Reed medical center.

hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes on Florida launchpad during test
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on the launchpad at Cape Canaveral in Florida during a scheduled test, dealing a significant setback to Jeff Bezos's spaceflight company and potentially jeopardizing NASA's ambitious lunar plans.

The explosion occurred at Launch Complex 36 during a "hotfire" test at 9 p.m. ET on Thursday. A massive fireball engulfed and destroyed the launchpad seconds after the test began. The blast was visible from miles away, with an orange sky reported in Fort Pierce, 115 miles south of the launch site, and a glow observed by residents in South Carolina hundreds of miles north. Shockwaves were felt across Florida's space coast, shaking homes in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach.

Blue Origin confirmed that all employees were safe and accounted for, with no injuries reported. The company described the incident as "an anomaly" and said it was already investigating the cause. Bezos acknowledged in a social media post that it was "a very rough day" but pledged to rebuild and return to flight operations.

The explosion threatens several major projects. NASA had just announced on Tuesday that Blue Origin won the contract to launch the first of three planned uncrewed lunar missions this year to begin construction of a 20 billion dollar moon base. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin intends to use for lunar landers, including those that will carry astronauts to the moon's surface.

The incident also affects NASA's Artemis program. The space agency is planning Artemis III for 2027 to test both Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander and SpaceX's competing lunar landing system. Both companies are competing for the contract to provide the lander for the Artemis IV mission planned for 2028, which would mark the first crewed lunar landing since 1972.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would conduct a full evaluation of project timelines following the explosion and work with Blue Origin to support a thorough investigation and assess mission impacts.

This test marked the first static fire test since the Federal Aviation Administration cleared the New Glenn rocket to resume flights following a previous mishap last month, when a payload from the rocket's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit.

The explosion comes as Blue Origin faces intensifying competition with SpaceX for government contracts and commercial launch services. SpaceX has maintained a steady launch schedule and continues to expand operations, including developing vehicles for NASA missions.

Launch Complex 36 has a long history supporting American spaceflight and will require repairs before it can support future launch attempts.

cards.headline: SpaceX awarded $4 billion Space Force contract for missile-tracking satellites
cards.teaser: The U.S. Space Force gave SpaceX a $4.16 billion contract to build a satellite network for tracking airborne targets.
cards.body:
The U.S. Space Force awarded SpaceX a $4.16 billion contract to develop satellite sensors for detecting and tracking airborne targets from space. The project, called Golden Dome, is linked to President Donald Trump's planned defense system and represents a significant expansion of SpaceX's role in military space capabilities.

This contract is part of SpaceX's growing government business. The company revealed in its IPO filing that government contracts already generated one-fifth of its 2025 revenue, underscoring the Pentagon's reliance on SpaceX for critical defense infrastructure.

cards.headline: Oil prices drop sharply on signs of U.S.-Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices fell and recorded the biggest monthly decline in six years as investors anticipated a potential U.S.-Iran deal.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell sharply Thursday after reports emerged of a potential breakthrough in U.S.-Iran talks that could extend a ceasefire. The decline reflects market expectations that an agreement might increase Iranian oil supplies, easing global supply constraints.

The price drops contributed to oil's largest monthly decline since 2020. Brent crude posted its worst month in several years, providing some relief to consumers at the pump as traders weighed the implications of the potential deal.

cards.headline: Universal Music rejects Bill Ackman's $64 billion takeover offer
cards.teaser: Universal Music Group declined a takeover proposal from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group rejected a $64 billion takeover bid from Pershing Square, the investment firm controlled by billionaire Bill Ackman. The music company said the offer fundamentally and materially undervalued the business.

Pershing Square is a shareholder in Universal Music Group. The company declined to accept the proposed acquisition price, signaling it believes the valuation does not reflect the true worth of its catalog and operations. Universal is one of the largest music companies globally, representing major artists and controlling significant music rights.

cards.headline: Southwest Airlines reverses policy on extra seats for plus-size passengers
cards.teaser: Southwest Airlines changed its seating policy for plus-size passengers after four months of pushback.
cards.body:
Southwest Airlines updated its policy regarding extra seats for plus-size passengers, rolling back a previous rule change that had generated criticism. The airline made the adjustment after receiving backlash for approximately four months.

The carrier modified its approach to accommodating passengers who require additional seating space. Southwest had previously altered its policy governing how it handles seat assignments for larger passengers, but the new rules proved divisive among customers and advocacy groups. The airline has now implemented different guidelines in response to the reaction.

cards.headline: Salmonella outbreak linked to moringa supplements sickens over 100 people
cards.teaser: More than 100 cases of salmonella have been tied to moringa capsules sold through major retailers including Amazon, Walmart, and Target.
cards.body:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is investigating a multistate salmonella outbreak connected to moringa supplements. Cases have been reported in eastern and western Washington state as well as other locations across the country, affecting more than 100 people.

The Food and Drug Administration has recalled the affected moringa capsules, which were sold through major online and retail platforms including Amazon, Walmart, and Target. Consumers who purchased these supplements are advised to discard any recalled products.

cards.headline: China's biotechnology industry challenges U.S. dominance in drug development
cards.teaser: Clinical trials from China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotech sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Chinese clinical trials are drawing significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago, signaling the country's expanding role in pharmaceutical innovation. China's growing biotechnology sector is raising concerns among industry observers about the future of American leadership in drug development.

China's substantial investments in biotech research have generated a rising number of clinical trials and drug candidates. This expansion is reshaping the global pharmaceutical landscape, with Chinese companies and researchers increasingly visible at major medical conferences and in scientific publications worldwide.

hero.headline: Court blocks US plan to relocate Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
hero.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked a plan by the Trump administration to relocate Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya. The ruling prevents the US from transferring individuals who may have been exposed to the virus to facilities in the African nation.

The United States has previously built specialized facilities specifically designed to handle cases involving potential Ebola exposure. These dedicated medical centers were created to isolate and treat individuals who may have contracted the disease while maintaining strict containment protocols.

The court decision comes as Kenya pushes back against the proposed arrangement, which would have seen the country accept Americans with potential Ebola exposure. The ruling represents a significant legal obstacle to the administration's plans for managing citizens who have been exposed to the deadly virus abroad.

Ebola is a severe and often fatal disease that spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids of infected individuals. The virus has caused multiple outbreaks in Africa over the past several decades, prompting international health agencies to develop strict protocols for handling exposed individuals.

The existence of purpose-built American facilities for Ebola cases raises questions about why the administration sought to relocate exposed individuals to Kenya instead of using domestic infrastructure. These specialized US centers were constructed with advanced isolation capabilities and trained medical personnel specifically for managing infectious disease cases like Ebola.

The Kenyan legal system's intervention highlights the diplomatic and legal complexities involved when governments attempt to transfer individuals with potential exposure to dangerous pathogens across international borders. The court's decision means the Trump administration will need to find alternative arrangements for managing Americans who have been exposed to Ebola while overseas, potentially including the use of existing American facilities that were built for exactly this purpose.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in new Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The contracts come as the company prepares for its initial public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX has received $6.45 billion in new contracts from the US Space Force as the company moves toward going public. The award underscores the importance of government spending to SpaceX's financial performance.

In its IPO filing, SpaceX disclosed that government contracts represented one-fifth of its total 2025 revenue. The contracts highlight how federal aerospace spending continues to be a major pillar of the company's business model.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling on Google ads draws support from company founders
cards.teaser: The decision could force platforms to change how they handle trademarked keywords in advertising.
cards.body:
An Indian court has ruled on Google's advertising practices regarding trademarked keywords, prompting renewed criticism from company founders who have long objected to how Google handles intellectual property in its ad system.

Legal experts say the decision could push online platforms to reconsider their policies on trademarked terms in advertisements. The ruling has gained backing from founders seeking to challenge Google's advertising business model.

cards.headline: Proposed federal rules would allow grant cancellations at any time
cards.teaser: The changes would also make peer review optional and let political staff screen research topics.
cards.body:
New proposed rules for US research funding would give agencies the power to cancel grants at any time, according to the draft regulations. The changes represent a major shift in how federal research money is managed and distributed.

The proposal would make peer review an optional step in the grant approval process rather than a standard requirement. Political staff would also gain authority to screen grant applications for forbidden topics, giving them a role in determining which research receives federal funding.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft tease laptop processor announcement
cards.teaser: The companies are pointing to new N1X laptop processors ahead of a computing event.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are publicly teasing the upcoming announcement of Nvidia's N1X laptop processors ahead of Computex this weekend. The Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts on X both posted "A new era of PC," with Arm following suit in the coordinated campaign.

Microsoft's Surface and Windows chief Pavan Davuluri also teased new hardware coming for developers, sharing a mysterious image of what appears to be a curved display edge. The simultaneous messaging from all three companies signals major announcements are imminent at the technology conference.

cards.headline: Apple Music experiences global service disruption
cards.teaser: The outage affected users in multiple countries before being resolved.
cards.body:
Apple Music suffered a service outage that affected users across multiple countries. The company confirmed the disruption to its streaming music platform, which prevented users from accessing the service.

Reports indicated that some users saw old albums flooding their recently added sections, while others experienced broken search functionality. Apple has since fixed the outage, which marked the third major service disruption for Apple Music streaming servers in two months.

cards.headline: Researchers warn AI code may not improve software quality
cards.teaser: Programmers who rely on AI tools produce code faster but not necessarily better, according to a new study.
cards.body:
Some programmers are refusing to work without AI assistance as the technology becomes standard in software development. Researchers have found that while AI helps coders write code more quickly, it may not be producing higher quality software.

The study authors warned that the speed gains from AI-assisted coding could create future problems if the code quality does not match the increased output. The findings raise questions about the long-term effects of widespread AI adoption in software engineering.

hero.headline: Golden Knights, Hurricanes to meet in Stanley Cup Final starting June 2
hero.body:
The NHL announced the Vegas Golden Knights will face the Carolina Hurricanes in the Stanley Cup Final, with Game 1 scheduled for June 2. The league also listed June 4 as a potential start date.

The series marks the Golden Knights' return to the championship round as they seek another title. Carolina will host the opening games of the series.

The NHL finalized the schedule after both conference finals concluded. The matchup brings together two teams that advanced through their respective playoff brackets to reach hockey's biggest stage.

The Hurricanes earned home-ice advantage for the first two games of the series. The exact game times and complete series schedule were released by the league alongside the announcement.

Both teams now have several days to prepare for the championship series. The Golden Knights previously competed in the Stanley Cup Final during their inaugural season in 2018, losing to the Washington Capitals. They won their first championship in 2023.

The Hurricanes last appeared in the Stanley Cup Final in 2006, when they defeated the Edmonton Oilers to claim the franchise's only championship. The team relocated from Hartford to Carolina in 1997.

The series will follow the standard 2-2-1-1-1 format, with Carolina hosting Games 1 and 2 before the series shifts to Vegas. If necessary, additional games would alternate between the two cities.

Vegas advanced through the Western Conference playoffs to reach the final, while Carolina won the Eastern Conference. Both teams completed their conference final series in time for the league to set the June 2 start date for the championship round.

cards.headline: Thunder's Jalen Williams ruled out for Western Conference Finals Game 7
cards.teaser: Oklahoma City will be without guard Jalen Williams for the decisive game against San Antonio.
cards.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder will be without guard Jalen Williams for Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals against the San Antonio Spurs due to a hamstring injury. Williams appeared in Game 6 but struggled, contributing just one point in the Thunder's 118-91 loss at San Antonio.

Game 7 takes place Saturday in Oklahoma City, with the winner advancing to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks. The Spurs dominated Game 6 behind Victor Wembanyama's 28 points and 10 rebounds, forcing the decisive seventh contest.

cards.headline: Canada names World Cup squad with Alphonso Davies
cards.teaser: Head coach Jesse Marsch selected Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies for the tournament roster.
cards.body:
Jesse Marsch, Canada's head coach, has selected Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies for the national team's World Cup squad this summer. Marsch called it the best Canada squad ever assembled for the tournament.

Davies' inclusion gives Canada an experienced defender from one of Europe's elite clubs as the team prepares for its first World Cup appearance since 1986.

cards.headline: Arsenal faces Paris Saint-Germain in Champions League final
cards.teaser: The two clubs will meet in the championship match on Saturday.
cards.body:
Arsenal will play Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final on Saturday, seeking the club's first European championship. Mikel Arteta's side has confirmed that Dutch defender Jurrien Timber is fit to start after recovering from a groin injury that sidelined him for over two months.

The match carries significant meaning for Arsenal's players. Several squad members have expressed their determination ahead of the final, viewing a victory as a landmark achievement for the club. Arsenal's path to the final came through the knockout rounds of Europe's premier club competition.

cards.headline: Jose Mourinho returns to Real Madrid as manager
cards.teaser: The Portuguese coach signed a deal to begin his second spell in charge of the Spanish club.
cards.body:
Jose Mourinho has agreed to return to Real Madrid as manager for a second spell with the club. His relationship with Brazil forward Vinicius Junior is expected to be one of the most closely watched aspects of his tenure.

Mourinho's first stint at Real Madrid ran from 2010 to 2013, during which he won La Liga and the Copa del Rey. He brings extensive experience managing top European clubs to his new role.

cards.headline: White Sox defeat Tigers 4-3 in 10 innings on Vargas walk-off home run
cards.teaser: Miguel Vargas hit his first career walk-off home run to win the game at home.
cards.body:
Miguel Vargas hit a walk-off home run in the 10th inning to lift the Chicago White Sox to a 4-3 victory over the Detroit Tigers. The blast was Vargas' first career walk-off hit and sent the packed crowd at the ballpark into celebration.

The game remained tied through nine innings before Vargas ended it with his extra-inning homer. The White Sox lost Munetaka Murakami during the game when he exited with a hamstring injury.

cards.headline: Novak Djokovic loses at French Open
cards.teaser: The 39-year-old exited the tournament in another setback at a Grand Slam event.
cards.body:
Novak Djokovic suffered a dramatic five-set defeat to Brazilian teenager João Fonseca at the French Open. Despite claiming the first two sets, the 39-year-old couldn't maintain his advantage, losing 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 in a grueling four-hour match on Court Philippe-Chatrier. The physical toll was evident as Djokovic struggled in the later stages against the 19-year-old opponent.

Fonseca's victory showcases the emergence of young talent challenging the sport's established names. The match highlighted the challenge facing aging champions as they compete against a new generation of players at Grand Slam level.

hero.headline: Star Wars Editor Marcia Lucas Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning editor of Star Wars and other films from the 1970s, died Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80.

Lucas died following a battle with metastatic cancer. Lucasfilm posted a statement mourning her death.

She was one of three editors to share an Academy Award for editing the original Star Wars film. Lucas also edited other notable films from the 1970s, including Taxi Driver.

Lucas was formerly married to Star Wars creator George Lucas. Her editing work helped shape some of the most influential films of the decade.

Lucasfilm described itself as deeply saddened by her death in its official statement released Friday. The studio acknowledged her contributions to the original Star Wars film, which became one of the most successful and culturally significant movies in cinema history.

The editing of Star Wars proved crucial to the film's success. Lucas worked alongside fellow editors Paul Hirsch and Richard Chew on the project. The three shared the Oscar for Best Film Editing at the 50th Academy Awards in 1978.

Her work on Taxi Driver, directed by Martin Scorsese and starring Robert De Niro, also earned critical acclaim. The film became one of the defining works of 1970s American cinema.

Lucas spent her final years in Rancho Mirage, a desert city in Riverside County, California. She had been battling metastatic cancer before her death on Wednesday.

The film industry has lost one of its pioneering editors from an era that transformed Hollywood filmmaking. Her technical skill and creative vision helped create two of the most enduring films from that period.

cards.headline: Music Executive Clive Davis Hospitalized in New York
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old music industry executive was admitted to a hospital Friday evening for a respiratory issue.
cards.body:
Clive Davis was hospitalized in New York City on Friday evening. The 94-year-old music executive was admitted for treatment of a respiratory issue.

Davis has been a major figure in the music industry for decades, working with numerous artists and helping shape popular music. He remains active in the industry despite his advanced age.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Rest of 2026 Tour Dates
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is stopping touring for the remainder of the year to focus on his health.
cards.body:
The 92-year-old legend announced Friday that he is canceling all remaining concert dates for 2026 to focus on his health. Valli, who has maintained an active touring schedule throughout his lengthy career, apologized to fans affected by the cancellations.

Despite his age, Valli has remained dedicated to performing and touring. The decision to step back reflects his prioritization of his wellbeing at this stage of his life.

cards.headline: Bill Maher Mocks Trump-Backed Freedom 250 Concert Series
cards.teaser: The HBO host dedicated a portion of his show Friday to the upcoming July 6 concert honoring America's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Bill Maher devoted part of his Friday night monologue on Real Time to President Trump's Freedom 250 concert series, scheduled for the National Mall in Washington, D.C., on July 6 to commemorate America's 250th anniversary.

The concert lineup has largely collapsed, with at least seven of nine featured musical acts withdrawing within 48 hours of the announcement. Bret Michaels, Morris Day, and Young MC were among those who dropped out, citing threats and a deteriorating atmosphere surrounding the event.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney Reflects on Family During Beatlemania
cards.teaser: The musician described how his family helped him navigate the Beatles' rise to fame and life under intense public attention.
cards.body:
Paul McCartney detailed how his family kept him grounded during the height of Beatlemania. The musician described a turning point during the Beatles' rise to fame in a recent interview.

McCartney explained how he navigated life under the spotlight as the band reached unprecedented levels of popularity. His family played a key role in helping him maintain perspective during that period.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Urges Governor Candidates to Support Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman called on gubernatorial candidates to back uncapped tax incentives for film and TV production in California.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman appeared outside Radford Studios on Friday to urge candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and television production. She was joined by entertainment figures including Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon, who support her mayoral campaign.

Raman said California must ensure Hollywood remains competitive. The appearance came in the final days before Tuesday's election. She emphasized the importance of the film industry to the state's economy.

cards.headline: Mountain Lion Tranquilized After Closing Santa Monica Street
cards.teaser: Wildlife officials tracked and tranquilized a mountain lion that closed 14th Street in Santa Monica for most of the day.
cards.body:
A mountain lion sighting in Santa Monica prompted officials to close 14th Street for most of the day. The animal was spotted in a residential neighborhood, putting the area on high alert.

Wildlife officials tracked the mountain lion through the neighborhood before tranquilizing it. The animal was found resting in a backyard of a Santa Monica home before being safely removed.

hero.headline: US military kills three in strike on suspected drug boat in eastern Pacific
hero.body:
The U.S. military carried out a strike on Friday against a boat accused of smuggling drugs in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing three men. U.S. Southern Command announced the action on the social platform X, stating that intelligence confirmed the vessel was traveling along known narco-trafficking routes and engaged in drug smuggling operations.

The command said the boat was operated by designated terrorist organizations, though it provided no evidence to support this claim. A 16-second video posted by Southern Command showed a single strike hitting the boat, which subsequently burst into flames. No U.S. military forces were harmed in the operation.

Friday's strike represents the third attack this week on suspected drug smuggling vessels. An earlier strike earlier in the week killed 11 people, making it one of the deadliest attacks this year. Since September, U.S. strikes on suspected drug-smuggling boats have killed at least 200 people.

These operations reflect an escalation under the Trump administration, which has increased U.S. military presence in the region to intercept drug traffickers. The strikes mark a shift from traditional interdiction methods, which typically involve boarding and seizing vessels suspected of smuggling narcotics.

However, the legality of these operations has drawn growing scrutiny from lawmakers and legal experts. Critics argue the Pentagon is conducting extrajudicial killings and abusing its power with life-or-death consequences.

"Under both U.S. and international law, it is flagrantly illegal to use the military to kill civilians suspected only of crimes," said Jeffrey Stein, a staff attorney with the American Civil Liberties Union, and Christopher Anders, director of the Democracy and Technology Division at the ACLU, in a December statement. "Civilians, including those suspected of smuggling drugs, are not lawful targets."

The debate over strike policy has also affected military leadership. Gen. Francis L. Donovan took over U.S. Southern Command after Admiral Alvin Holsey abruptly retired, reportedly over disagreements about the strike policy. Southern Command oversees U.S. military operations in Latin America and the Caribbean, conducting counter-narcotics missions as part of its regional security mandate.

The eastern Pacific corridor serves as a major transit route for drug smuggling operations attempting to move narcotics northward through Central America and Mexico. Southern Command has not provided information about the nationalities of the three men killed, whether any drugs were recovered from the vessel, or additional details about the specific terrorist organizations allegedly operating the boat.

cards.headline: White House releases memo saying Trump in excellent health after physical
cards.teaser: President Trump's physician released a memo saying the president remains in excellent health following his annual physical exam.
cards.body:
President Trump's physician released a memo through the White House confirming the president remains in excellent health following his annual physical exam at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center earlier this week. The examination included cardiac, neurological, and dermatologic assessments.

The White House released the physician's memo late Friday. However, independent physicians have raised questions about recurrent bruises on Trump's hands and swelling in his legs.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Pam Evette for South Carolina governor over Nancy Mace
cards.teaser: President Trump backed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina governor's race, bypassing Rep. Nancy Mace.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina gubernatorial race, publicly backing her over Rep. Nancy Mace, who is also seeking the Republican nomination. Trump announced his support on Friday through a post on Truth Social.

In his endorsement message, Trump praised Evette as an "America First Patriot" who remained steadfast in her principles. He characterized her as a good friend, fighter, and winner.

cards.headline: Federal judge agrees to reopen Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit
cards.teaser: A federal judge in Florida sided with intervenors who said a settlement creating an anti-weaponization fund tainted Trump's case against the IRS.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida has agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The judge sided with intervenors who challenged a settlement agreement between the Department of Justice and Trump that would have dismissed the case in exchange for creating an "anti-weaponization" fund.

Meanwhile, a federal judge in Virginia temporarily blocked the Trump administration from transferring money into the $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund while legal challenges to it proceed. The order prevents funds from being disbursed while arguments continue in the case challenging the fund's creation and operation.

cards.headline: Southern Command chief meets with Cuban military officials
cards.teaser: The head of U.S. Southern Command met with senior Cuban military leaders near Guantanamo Bay amid heightened tensions between the two governments.
cards.body:
The head of U.S. Southern Command met with senior leaders of the Cuban military amid heightened tensions between the two countries' governments. Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan joined Cuba's First Deputy Minister of the Chief of the General Staff Roberto Legra Sotolongo and other leaders near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay.

Southern Command announced the meeting on Friday. The session took place as tensions between the U.S. and Cuban governments have increased.

cards.headline: Talarico leads Paxton by 3 points in Texas Senate race poll
cards.teaser: State Rep. James Talarico holds a slight edge over Attorney General Ken Paxton in a new poll of likely general election voters.
cards.body:
State Rep. James Talarico leads in the Texas Senate race according to a new poll released Friday. Forty-seven percent of likely general election voters in the state backed Talarico in the poll from Texas Public Opinion Research, compared with 44 percent for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

The poll shows the Democratic candidate with a three-point advantage over his Republican opponent following the runoff elections. The survey measured support among likely voters in the general election.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary Bessent endorses putting Trump on proposed $250 bill
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent said President Trump should appear on a proposed $250 bill to commemorate the U.S. semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent endorsed a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait to commemorate the U.S. semiquincentennial. Speaking at a White House news conference, Bessent said the bill would celebrate the country's 250th anniversary of independence. The treasury has already begun preparing for the possibility of the new currency.

The proposal would require changing federal law that currently prohibits any living person from appearing on U.S. currency. While the White House is pushing Congress to approve the measure, Democrats have vowed to block the move.
